# A name-constrained private root: root_cert (self-signed, serial 1) carries a critical nameConstraints extension
# permitting only DNS:corp.example. in_scope_leaf_cert (serial 2, SAN DNS:app.corp.example) is within it;
# out_of_scope_leaf_cert (serial 3, SAN DNS:bank.example) is validly signed by the root but outside it.
# Validity 2020-01-01..2099-12-31, ecdsa-with-SHA256, leaves carry EKU serverAuth+clientAuth.
# Generated with OpenSSL 4.0.1 (NB=20200101000000Z, NA=20991231000000Z; MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'):
#   openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out X.key   (root, leaf1, leaf2)
#   openssl req -new -x509 -key root.key -sha256 -subj "/CN=TlsLib NameConstrained Root" -set_serial 1 -not_before NB -not_after NA
#     -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE" -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" -addext "subjectKeyIdentifier=hash"
#     -addext "nameConstraints=critical,permitted;DNS:corp.example" -out root.pem
#   openssl req -new -key leafN.key -subj "/CN=<san>" -out leafN.csr
#   openssl x509 -req -in leafN.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -set_serial N -sha256 -not_before NB -not_after NA -extfile leafN.ext -out leafN.pem
#     leafN.ext: basicConstraints=CA:false / keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature / extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth,clientAuth / subjectAltName=DNS:<san> /
#                subjectKeyIdentifier=hash / authorityKeyIdentifier=keyid
#   openssl verify -CAfile root.pem leaf1.pem (OK; openssl rejects leaf2 for the name constraint);  openssl x509 -in X.pem -outform DER | xxd -p
root_
in_scope_leaf_
out_of_scope_leaf_
